problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B={{B}_{1},{B}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & {x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1} & -3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}=4 \\ -3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=8.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ -3 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ -3 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 6 & 6 \\ 0 & 11 & 11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 6{x}_{2}=6 \\ 11{x}_{2}=11.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second,  third and fourth equations, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3\cdot 1 & =1 \\ {x}_{1} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-2)+1=-1.$
